name: Atmosphere
tagline: The ocean of air — layers, composition, ISA

rows.label: Troposphere
rows.info: Surface to ~36,000 ft · all weather occurs here · temperature decreases at 2°C/1,000 ft

rows.label: Tropopause
rows.info: Thin boundary at ~36,000 ft · temperature stops decreasing · jet stream located here

rows.label: Stratosphere
rows.info: ~36,000–160,000 ft · very stable · temperature constant then rises due to ozone absorption

rows.label: Above stratosphere
rows.info: Mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere — no operational aviation significance

rows.label: Nitrogen (N₂)
rows.info: 78% of dry atmosphere — inert, not consumed by combustion

rows.label: Oxygen (O₂)
rows.info: 21% — required for combustion and respiration

rows.label: Other
rows.info: 1% — argon, CO₂, water vapor, trace gases

rows.label: Sea Level Temperature
rows.info: 15°C (59°F) — decreases 2°C per 1,000 ft to tropopause

rows.label: Sea Level Pressure
rows.info: 29.92 in Hg / 1013.25 hPa — decreases approximately 1 in Hg per 1,000 ft

rows.label: Speed of Sound
rows.info: 661 KTAS at MSL — decreases with altitude due to lower temperature

rows.label: Standard Day
rows.info: All aircraft performance data is based on ISA — real conditions nearly always differ

rows.label: High Pressure (H)
rows.info: Descending/sinking air · diverges from center · clockwise circulation (NH) · generally fair weather

rows.label: Low Pressure (L)
rows.info: Rising air · converges at center · counterclockwise (NH) · clouds, precipitation, bad weather

rows.label: Pressure Gradient
rows.info: Rate of pressure change over distance · closely-spaced isobars = stronger winds

rows.label: Isobars
rows.info: Lines of equal pressure on surface analysis charts · wind flows nearly parallel to them

rows.label: Altimeter Setting
rows.info: Adjusts altimeter to local sea-level pressure so indicated altitude matches actual MSL altitude

rows.label: "High to Low Look Out Below"
rows.info: Flying from high to low pressure without updating altimeter: aircraft is lower than indicated

rows.label: Pressure Altitude
rows.info: Altitude indicated with altimeter set to 29.92 in Hg · used for all aircraft performance tables

rows.label: Class A Operation
rows.info: All aircraft set 29.92 above 18,000 MSL — FL altitudes eliminate setting differences

rows.label: Definition
rows.info: Pressure altitude corrected for non-standard temperature · the altitude the aircraft 'thinks' it's at

rows.label: Increases with
rows.info: ↑ temperature, ↑ field elevation, ↑ humidity

rows.label: Effect on performance
rows.info: Reduced engine power, reduced prop efficiency, longer takeoff roll, reduced climb rate

rows.label: Hot/High/Humid (Triple H)
rows.info: Density altitude can far exceed field elevation — performance charts are mandatory, not optional

rows.label: Rule of thumb
rows.info: Density alt rises ~120 ft per °C above ISA (roughly)

name: Temperature
tagline: Heat transfer, lapse rates, and inversions

rows.label: Radiation
rows.info: Energy from sun heats earth's surface directly

rows.label: Conduction
rows.info: Transfer through direct contact — surface heats adjacent air molecules

rows.label: Convection
rows.info: Vertical movement of air transporting heat — thermals, columns of rising air

rows.label: Advection
rows.info: Horizontal transport of heat (or cold) via moving air masses

rows.label: Environmental (ELR)
rows.info: Actual temperature change measured in the existing atmosphere — varies by day and location

rows.label: Dry Adiabatic (DALR)
rows.info: 3°C / 1,000 ft — unsaturated parcel cools at this rate as it rises

rows.label: Moist/Saturated Adiabatic (SALR)
rows.info: ~1.5°C / 1,000 ft — saturated parcel releases latent heat, cools slower

rows.label: Standard (ISA)
rows.info: 2°C / 1,000 ft — average used for navigation, altimeter settings, performance data

rows.label: Definition
rows.info: Temperature increases with altitude — opposite of normal · creates very stable layer

rows.label: Effect on aircraft
rows.info: Wind shear often present at the top · visibility can be poor below (trapped smoke/haze)

rows.label: Radiation Inversion
rows.info: Forms overnight via surface cooling · clear sky + calm wind + moist air = fog in valleys

rows.label: Subsidence Inversion
rows.info: Sinking air in high-pressure centers warms adiabatically · caps convection, traps pollutants

rows.label: Frontal Inversion
rows.info: Warm air riding over cold at frontal boundary — ceiling and visibility change at inversion level

name: Moisture & Clouds
tagline: Humidity, dew point, cloud families, precipitation

rows.label: Relative Humidity
rows.info: Ratio of actual moisture to maximum possible at that temperature — expressed as %

rows.label: Dew Point
rows.info: Temperature to which air must cool (at constant pressure) to become saturated and begin condensing

rows.label: T/Td Spread
rows.info: Temperature minus dew point — smaller spread means more moisture; < 4°F = fog or low cloud risk

rows.label: Condensation Nuclei
rows.info: Tiny particles (dust, sea salt, smoke) that water vapor condenses on to form cloud droplets

rows.label: High (16,500–45,000 ft)
rows.info: Cirrus (Ci), Cirrostratus (Cs), Cirrocumulus (Cc) · ice crystals only · no significant precipitation

rows.label: Middle (6,500–23,000 ft)
rows.info: Altostratus (As), Altocumulus (Ac) · mixed ice and water · light precipitation possible

rows.label: Low (surface–6,500 ft)
rows.info: Stratus (St), Stratocumulus (Sc), Nimbostratus (Ns) · liquid water · steady rain/drizzle from Ns

rows.label: Vertical development
rows.info: Cumulus (Cu), Cumulonimbus (Cb) · span multiple levels · indicate instability · Cb = thunderstorm

rows.label: Cumulus
rows.info: Heaped/puffy — unstable air, vertical development

rows.label: Stratus
rows.info: Layered/sheet — stable air, horizontal development

rows.label: Cirrus
rows.info: High, wispy ice crystals — prefix for high clouds

rows.label: Nimbus
rows.info: Rain-bearing — Nimbostratus (steady) or Cumulonimbus (convective)

rows.label: Alto
rows.info: Middle level prefix — Altostratus, Altocumulus

rows.label: Drizzle
rows.info: Drops < 0.5 mm · from stratus clouds · significantly reduces visibility

rows.label: Rain / Showers
rows.info: Rain: steady from Ns · Showers: intermittent from Cb/Cu — start/stop abruptly

rows.label: Freezing Rain / Drizzle
rows.info: Supercooled drops freeze on contact — severe icing hazard for aircraft

rows.label: Snow
rows.info: Ice crystals — reduces visibility · accumulates on surfaces

rows.label: Hail
rows.info: Ice pellets formed in thunderstorm updrafts — can extend 2+ nm from storm

rows.label: Virga
rows.info: Precipitation that evaporates before reaching the ground — visible streamers from cloud base

name: Fog
tagline: Five types — same result, different causes

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: Clear sky + calm/light winds (< 5 kt) + moist surface air + nighttime radiational cooling

rows.label: Location
rows.info: Valleys and low areas — cold dense air drains downslope · thickest near sunrise

rows.label: Dissipation
rows.info: Burns off after sunrise from the top down · may lift to low stratus layer first

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: Warm moist air moves horizontally over a colder surface and cools to dew point

rows.label: Location
rows.info: Common on Pacific coast, Great Lakes, coastal areas year-round

rows.label: Key difference
rows.info: Requires wind (unlike radiation) · can be extensive and persistent for days · forms day or night

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: Moist air forced up terrain slope and cools adiabatically to its dew point

rows.label: Location
rows.info: East slopes of Rockies, Appalachians — requires easterly wind flow uphill

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: Cold, dry air moves over warm water — water evaporates and condenses immediately above the surface

rows.label: Location
rows.info: Lakes and coastal areas in fall/winter — appears as steam rising

rows.label: Hazard
rows.info: Associated with low-level turbulence and icing conditions

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: Warm rain falls through sub-freezing air ahead of a warm/stationary front · evaporates and saturates cold air below

rows.label: Extent
rows.info: Widespread and persistent · serious IFR hazard along warm or stationary fronts for hundreds of miles

name: Stability
tagline: What resists vertical motion — or what triggers explosive convection

rows.label: Absolutely Stable
rows.info: ELR < SALR · rising parcel always cooler than surroundings · resists all vertical motion

rows.label: Conditionally Unstable
rows.info: SALR < ELR < DALR · stable when unsaturated, unstable once saturated · most common state

rows.label: Absolutely Unstable
rows.info: ELR > DALR · parcel always warmer than environment — uncontrolled violent convection

rows.label: Orographic
rows.info: Air forced over terrain · windward side: clouds and precip · lee side: warming and drying (foehn/chinook)

rows.label: Frontal
rows.info: Dense cold air undercuts warm air mass · forces warm air upward along frontal slope

rows.label: Convective
rows.info: Surface heating creates thermals — columns of rising warm air · peak in afternoon

rows.label: Convergence
rows.info: Surface winds from different directions converge, forcing air aloft · common in low pressure centers

rows.label: Stable signs
rows.info: Stratus clouds · steady widespread precipitation · smooth air · reduced visibility (haze/smoke trapped below inversion)

rows.label: Unstable signs
rows.info: Growing towering Cu (TCu) · cumulonimbus · showery precipitation · excellent visibility · turbulent air

rows.label: Developing instability
rows.info: Cumulus bases lowering and tops rising through the day → afternoon thunderstorm risk

name: Thunderstorms
tagline: Never penetrate — always avoid by 20 nm

rows.label: Moisture
rows.info: Sufficient water vapor — maritime tropical (mT) air masses are primary fuel

rows.label: Lifting Force
rows.info: Frontal, orographic, convective, or convergence lifting to initiate vertical development

rows.label: Instability
rows.info: Unstable atmosphere that allows a lifted parcel to continue rising on its own

rows.label: 1. Cumulus Stage
rows.info: Updrafts only · cloud building rapidly · no lightning or precipitation yet

rows.label: 2. Mature Stage
rows.info: Most intense · updrafts AND downdrafts coexist · lightning · heavy precipitation · hail · most dangerous

rows.label: 3. Dissipating Stage
rows.info: Downdrafts dominate · rain tapering · anvil may persist · can still be severe near mature cells nearby

rows.label: Air Mass (Single-Cell)
rows.info: Local surface heating · isolated · short-lived (< 1 hr) · peaks late afternoon

rows.label: Frontal / Squall Line
rows.info: Along or ahead of cold fronts · fast-moving · severe weather · extensive coverage

rows.label: Orographic
rows.info: Forced lifting over mountains · can be stationary relative to terrain

rows.label: Supercell
rows.info: Long-lived rotating storm · produces largest hail, strongest tornadoes, extreme winds

rows.label: Embedded (Squall Line)
rows.info: Hidden inside stratiform clouds · no visual warning · detected by radar or PIREP only — most dangerous to encounter

rows.label: Severe Turbulence
rows.info: Extends up to 20 nm from storm in clear air · severe to extreme intensity

rows.label: Hail
rows.info: Can fall 2+ nm from visible cloud edge · clear air above — no visual warning

rows.label: Microbursts
rows.info: Intense concentrated downdraft (up to 6,000 fpm) · severe wind shear on approach below 1,000 ft AGL

rows.label: Lightning
rows.info: Strikes aircraft directly · induced electrical surges damage avionics and fuel systems

rows.label: Low-Level Wind Shear
rows.info: Sudden airspeed loss on approach — if you gain airspeed then lose it rapidly, go around immediately

rows.label: Structural Icing
rows.info: Severe icing in updraft regions at −0°C to −20°C · supercooled large drops above that

rows.label: Tornadoes
rows.info: Most violent weather phenomenon · especially from supercell thunderstorms

rows.label: Horizontal avoidance
rows.info: At least 20 nm from any active thunderstorm · hail and CAT extend well beyond visible cloud

rows.label: Never fly under the anvil
rows.info: Hail, severe turbulence, and downbursts occur beneath the anvil of active cells

rows.label: Never penetrate a CB
rows.info: There is no safe thunderstorm — avoid any cumulonimbus of any intensity

rows.label: Microbursts
rows.info: Maximum intensity at 100–300 ft AGL · wet or dry (dry microbursts are invisible) · radius 1–2 nm · last 5–15 min

name: Icing
tagline: Structural and carburetor — both kill performance

rows.label: Both conditions required
rows.info: Visible moisture (cloud, rain, drizzle, fog) AND OAT at or below 0°C (32°F)

rows.label: Most hazardous range
rows.info: 0°C to −20°C where supercooled large drops (SLD) exist in greatest concentration

rows.label: Above −40°C
rows.info: All water has frozen to ice crystals — risk greatly reduced; aircraft can fly through without accumulation

rows.label: Clear Ice
rows.info: Large supercooled drops freeze slowly — smooth, hard, transparent · heaviest accumulation · most dangerous · hardest to shed

rows.label: Rime Ice
rows.info: Small drops freeze instantly — rough, opaque, white, brittle · lighter than clear · less lift disruption but still dangerous

rows.label: Mixed Ice
rows.info: Combination of both — irregular shape, rough surface, difficult to remove · common in clouds with varying drop sizes

rows.label: Lift loss
rows.info: Disrupts smooth airflow over wing — ½ inch of clear ice can reduce lift by 30% or more

rows.label: Drag increase
rows.info: Rough surface dramatically increases parasite drag

rows.label: Weight
rows.info: Ice adds hundreds of pounds rapidly — reduces useful load and climb performance

rows.label: Control loss
rows.info: Ice on control surfaces reduces effectiveness and may cause flutter or airframe damage

rows.label: Pitot/static blockage
rows.info: Iced pitot tube → erroneous/stuck airspeed; iced static port → erroneous altimeter + VSI

rows.label: How it forms
rows.info: Fuel vaporization + venturi effect drops temperature 15–25°C · ice forms on throttle plate and venturi

rows.label: Conditions
rows.info: OAT −7°C to +21°C (20°F–70°F) + high relative humidity · can form in clear air

rows.label: Symptom (fixed-pitch)
rows.info: Unexplained RPM decrease

rows.label: Symptom (constant-speed)
rows.info: Manifold pressure drop with no RPM change

rows.label: Treatment
rows.info: Apply FULL carburetor heat · engine may run rough briefly as ice melts — this is normal, wait for RPM to recover

rows.label: Prevention
rows.info: Use carb heat during low power (descent), in high humidity, near dew point · check POH placard for guidance

name: Turbulence
tagline: Thermals, shear, mountains, clear air — always report PIREPs

keyStats.label: CAT location
keyStats.value: Near jet stream, no visual cue

rows.label: Light
rows.info: Slight erratic changes in altitude/attitude · occupants may feel slight strain against seatbelts

rows.label: Moderate
rows.info: Similar to light but more intense · aircraft fully controllable · unsecured items displaced

rows.label: Severe
rows.info: Large abrupt changes · possible brief loss of control · occupants forced hard against restraints · injury possible

rows.label: Extreme
rows.info: Aircraft practically impossible to control · structural damage likely · very rare

rows.label: Convective (Thermal)
rows.info: Solar heating creates rising/sinking columns · below and near cumulus clouds · peaks in afternoon

rows.label: Mechanical
rows.info: Wind flowing over rough terrain, buildings, trees · intensity increases with wind speed

rows.label: Wind Shear
rows.info: Abrupt change in wind speed/direction over short distance · near fronts, inversions, jet stream

rows.label: Mountain Wave
rows.info: Standing wave in lee of mountains · rotor zone extremely turbulent · can persist 100s of nm downwind

rows.label: Clear Air (CAT)
rows.info: No visual cue · near jet stream, tropopause · fast and sudden · abrupt changes alert crew

rows.label: Wake Turbulence
rows.info: Wingtip vortices from large aircraft · descend and move upwind · stay above and upwind of large aircraft flight path

rows.label: Lenticular (ACSL) clouds
rows.info: Stationary lens-shaped clouds at wave crests — they mark the wave, NOT where the turbulence is worst

rows.label: Rotor zone
rows.info: In the lee below wave crest — extremely severe/extreme turbulence · can break up aircraft

rows.label: Cap cloud
rows.info: Clouds over mountain peak — air is accelerating through; severe turbulence and icing

rows.label: Extent
rows.info: Wave can reach 5× mountain height and extend hundreds of nm downwind

rows.label: Conditions for formation
rows.info: Wind 20+ kt perpendicular to ridge · wind speed increases with altitude · stable layer above mountain top

name: Wind
tagline: Global circulation, jet stream, and local effects

rows.label: Coriolis Effect
rows.info: Earth's rotation deflects moving air — right in Northern Hemisphere, left in Southern Hemisphere

rows.label: Trade Winds
rows.info: Northeast (NH) / Southeast (SH) surface winds · 0°–30° latitude · toward the ITCZ

rows.label: Westerlies
rows.info: Prevailing surface westerlies 30°–60° latitude — U.S. weather moves west to east because of this

rows.label: Polar Easterlies
rows.info: Cold dry air flows from poles toward 60° latitude

rows.label: Polar Jet
rows.info: Strongest jet · 30,000–40,000 ft · average 100–200 kt · meanders N-S with seasons · affects most U.S. flight plans

rows.label: Subtropical Jet
rows.info: Weaker · 25,000–35,000 ft · more stable location year-round

rows.label: CAT risk
rows.info: Severe turbulence near jet core edges — especially where wind shear is greatest

rows.label: Navigation
rows.info: Ride the jet tailwind eastbound · avoid or route around westbound to save fuel and time

rows.label: Friction layer
rows.info: Surface to ~2,000 AGL — friction slows wind speed and causes backing (counterclockwise direction shift in NH)

rows.label: Wind shear through friction layer
rows.info: Significant speed and direction change from runway to 2,000 AGL — critical for takeoff/landing performance

rows.label: Sea Breeze
rows.info: Daytime — land heats faster than water → low pressure onshore → cool sea air flows inland

rows.label: Land Breeze
rows.info: Nighttime — land cools faster → cool air drains seaward · typically gentler than sea breeze

rows.label: Valley/Mountain Breeze
rows.info: Anabatic (day): valley heats → air rises up slopes · Katabatic (night): cool air drains down into valleys

rows.label: Chinook / Santa Ana
rows.info: Dry warm downslope winds — can gust violently at terrain base, cause fire risk, significant low-level turbulence

rows.label: Definition
rows.info: Any abrupt change in wind speed or direction over a short distance — horizontal or vertical

rows.label: Low-level wind shear (LLWS)
rows.info: Most critical — below 2,000 ft AGL on approach or departure · from fronts, thunderstorms, inversions

rows.label: Microburst wind shear
rows.info: Headwind → downdraft → tailwind in sequence on approach = rapidly decreasing performance

rows.label: Recovery
rows.info: Immediate full power, pitch up, escape the shear — do not try to salvage the approach

name: Air Masses & Fronts
tagline: Boundaries between air masses drive most NAS weather

rows.label: cA / cP (continental Arctic/Polar)
rows.info: Cold, dry, stable · originates over land (Canada/Alaska) · clear weather but cold

rows.label: mP (maritime Polar)
rows.info: Cool, moist · from N. Pacific or N. Atlantic · stratus, drizzle, low ceilings on coasts

rows.label: cT (continental Tropical)
rows.info: Hot, dry, unstable · from SW U.S. / Mexico desert in summer · good visibility but high density altitude

rows.label: mT (maritime Tropical)
rows.info: Warm, moist, unstable · from Gulf/Caribbean · primary thunderstorm fuel for U.S. · poor visibility in haze

rows.label: Structure
rows.info: Cold dense air wedges under warmer air · steep slope (1:50 to 1:100) · fast-moving

rows.label: Weather (fast-moving)
rows.info: Narrow squall line of CB, heavy showers, thunderstorms · severe but brief · excellent visibility after passage

rows.label: Weather (slow-moving)
rows.info: Broader area of clouds and precipitation · embedded CB · worse than fast fronts for IFR

rows.label: After passage
rows.info: Temperature drops sharply · pressure rises · winds veer clockwise (NH) · visibility improves dramatically

rows.label: Structure
rows.info: Warm air overrides slower cold air · gradual slope (1:100 to 1:200) · extensive cloud deck ahead

rows.label: Cloud sequence (250+ nm ahead)
rows.info: Cirrus → Cirrostratus (halo) → Altostratus → Nimbostratus — ceiling lowers progressively

rows.label: Weather below
rows.info: Steady widespread precipitation for hundreds of miles · low ceilings · poor visibility · IFR for extended periods

rows.label: Freezing rain hazard
rows.info: Warm rain falls through sub-freezing air below front — severe widespread icing at all altitudes below the frontal slope

rows.label: After passage
rows.info: Temperature rises · humidity remains high · visibility may still be limited in haze and low stratus

rows.label: Stationary Front
rows.info: Movement < 5 kt · IFR conditions can persist for days over a large area — the worst scenario for VFR planning

rows.label: Occluded Front (Cold Type)
rows.info: Fast cold front catches warm front · complex weather extending through the troposphere

rows.label: Dry Line
rows.info: Not a temperature boundary — moisture boundary in the Great Plains · explosive thunderstorm trigger (not on most charts)

name: Weather Products
tagline: Know your sources — from METAR to Convective SIGMET

rows.label: METAR
rows.info: Aviation Routine Weather Report · issued hourly · surface obs at airports (wind, vis, sky, temp, dewpoint, altimeter)

rows.label: SPECI
rows.info: Special METAR issued when significant change occurs (below IFR minimums, wind shift, precip onset, etc.)

rows.label: AWOS / ASOS
rows.info: Automated stations · continuous reporting · some require pilot-only input (AWSS) · verify via Notam for outages

rows.label: PIREP (UA / UUA)
rows.info: Pilot Reports · UA = routine · UUA = urgent · only real-time source of in-flight weather across many routes — file them

rows.label: TAF
rows.info: Terminal Aerodrome Forecast · 24–30 hr window · within 5 SM radius of airport · issued 4×/day

rows.label: GFA (Graphical Forecast for Aviation)
rows.info: Replaces FA for CONUS · graphical depiction of clouds, precip, turbulence, icing · 12-hr forecasts

rows.label: Winds and Temps Aloft (FB)
rows.info: Forecast winds/temps at 3,000–53,000 ft at multiple stations · issued 4×/day · essential for fuel planning

rows.label: Prog Charts
rows.info: 12/24/36/48-hr surface/upper-level forecast · isobars, fronts, pressure systems

rows.label: SIGMET (WS)
rows.info: Significant Met Info · non-convective · covers severe/extreme turbulence, severe icing, volcanic ash, sand storms · 4-hr valid

rows.label: Convective SIGMET (WST)
rows.info: Thunderstorm activity · issued hourly or special · always valid for all aircraft · supersedes all other convective advisories

rows.label: AIRMET Sierra (WA)
rows.info: IFR conditions (ceilings < 1,000 ft / vis < 3 SM) and/or mountain obscuration · 6-hr valid · critical for VFR flight

rows.label: AIRMET Tango (WA)
rows.info: Moderate turbulence, sustained surface winds > 30 kt, low-level wind shear · 6-hr valid

rows.label: AIRMET Zulu (WA)
rows.info: Moderate icing and freezing levels · 6-hr valid

rows.label: CWA (Center Weather Advisory)
rows.info: Issued by ARTCCs for imminent or existing weather within 2 hrs · highly localized and specific · very useful in-flight

rows.label: NEXRAD Radar
rows.info: National Doppler radar network · shows precipitation intensity (dBZ) and type · foundation of weather avoidance

rows.label: ADS-B / FIS-B Datalink
rows.info: Delivers NEXRAD to cockpit for free via ADS-B In · ALWAYS 5–20 minutes delayed — NOT for direct storm avoidance

rows.label: Satellite Imagery
rows.info: Visible (daytime) and IR (day/night) · IR shows cloud-top temperatures from which cloud heights are estimated

rows.label: Skew-T / Sounding
rows.info: Upper-air analysis · shows actual lapse rates, freezing levels, wind shear by altitude, CB potential (CAPE, LI)
